title: A token submessage comes back with the exact same format, subformat and content

provenance.quote: If any NLIP message containing a submessage that where the format field is 'token', the end-point must include the same submessage with the exact same format, subformat and content in its response message to the peer end-point, except when the token was initially created by the end-point.

notes: Three things are asserted at once, and all three are the words "exact same". The subformat keeps its mixed case: §5 makes the *format* value case-insensitive and says nothing that would let an end-point rewrite an opaque one. The content keeps every byte, including the `/` and `+` that a base64-guessing implementation might try to normalise. And `Group_Alpha` is neither of §5.3's two reserved prefixes — §6.2 ¶4 allows "any general string" and conditions the echo on nothing — so a token an end-point cannot interpret still comes back. The reply's own first submessage stays the end-point's answer: §6.2 ¶2 asks for the submessage and says nothing about where it goes, while §5.1.4 has already spoken for the first one. `authority.own` is empty, so the exception does not apply to anything here. `withheld` is `false` and is asserted for one reason: it is the corpus's ordinary value, and a flag only ever pinned where it is `true` would pass an implementation that always answered `true` — `readings/45` and `/46` are the other half.
